label: Bok Choy
note: Covers 'bok choy' / 'bok-choy' / 'pak choi'. Baby bok choy matches the same token and is wanted per the candidate notes. Napa cabbage never carries a bok-choy token; frozen stir-fry blends excluded (global frozen also blocks). No existing commodity matches these tokens.

label: Butternut Squash
note: Whole squash only: candidate notes exclude the pre-cut cubed convenience SKU, so cubed/cut/diced/chunks/spirals/noodles all excluded. Soup and frozen are global-blocked anyway; kept locally for clarity. Zucchini's include (zucchini | yellow squash) cannot touch this phrase.

label: Acorn Squash
note: Full phrase 'acorn squash' cannot collide with butternut/spaghetti (separate candidates) or zucchini/yellow squash (existing). Per-each store pricing normalized to lb downstream.

label: Spaghetti Squash
note: HIJACK FLAG: existing 'pasta' includes bare 'spaghetti', which substring-matches 'Spaghetti Squash', and pasta's excludes have no squash token - pasta steals every spaghetti squash today. Fix in collisions-b.md (add \bsquash\b to pasta exclude). This rule requires the full 'spaghetti squash' phrase so it can never steal pasta; spaghetti sauce / SpaghettiOs lack the word squash.

label: Sugar Snap Peas
note: HIJACK FLAG (blocking): existing 'snow-peas' explicitly includes 'sugar\s+snap\s+peas' AND '\bsnap\s+peas', so it first-match-steals every sugar snap product; this commodity gets nothing until snow-peas adds a 'sugar\s+snap' exclude (see collisions-b.md). Excludes mirror snow-peas' own snack-crisp guards. Frozen sugar snaps and canned/frozen peas cannot enter (global + phrase).

label: Spring Mix Salad Greens
note: RELAX_GLOBAL required: the product name 'Spring Mix' trips the global '\bmix\b(?!\s*(?:&|and)\s*match)' token; relaxed exactly that token. '50/50' covers the spinach + spring mix blend - but existing 'spinach' (bare include) currently first-match-steals any 50/50 title containing the word spinach; fix in collisions-b.md. Kits with dressing excluded; spinach-only and arugula-only packs cannot match these phrases.

label: Arugula
note: Arugula-only packs per the candidate: blends/spring-mix/50-50/kits excluded so multi-green products route to spring-mix instead. 'spinach' excluded because arugula-spinach duo packs belong to neither pure item (and existing spinach would first-match them anyway). Pizza/pesto guard prepared foods that name arugula.

label: Garden Salad Blend (bagged)
note: RELAX_GLOBAL required: common titles like 'Classic/Garden Salad Mix' trip the global mix token. HIJACK FLAG: existing 'lettuce' includes \biceberg\b and none of its excludes (kit/blend/shredded/chopped/salad mix) hit 'Classic Iceberg Salad' bags - lettuce steals them; fix in collisions-b.md. pasta/macaroni/potato excludes stop deli 'garden pasta/potato salad' tubs; kits with dressing route to the kit item.

label: Caesar Salad Kit
note: RELAX_GLOBAL required: every product title carries 'kit', a global-excluded token; relaxed exactly '\bkit\b'. Includes demand the word caesar, so other-flavor chopped-salad kits stay out per the candidate. Bottled caesar dressing lacks 'kit'/'complete caesar' and existing caesar-dressing already excludes kit both ways - no collision. 'chicken'/'bowl' block prepared caesar meals.

label: Coleslaw Mix
note: RELAX_GLOBAL required: 'Coleslaw Mix' trips the global mix token. Prepared deli coleslaw tubs are titled without 'mix'/'shredded' so they cannot match; dressing bottles excluded; broccoli slaw excluded per candidate. Existing 'cabbage' excludes slaw/shredded and 'sauerkraut' excludes slaw, so neither steals from nor loses to this rule.

label: Stir-Fry Vegetable Blend (fresh)
note: CRITICAL: '\bfrozen\b' excluded locally AND globally - frozen stir-fry bags are a different item (existing frozen-vegetables relaxes frozen for itself but its includes don't cover stir-fry, so no overlap either way). RELAX_GLOBAL for the mix token because some produce blends are titled 'Stir Fry Mix'. Meat-word and noodle/sauce/kit excludes keep meal kits out. Titles naming water chestnuts get dropped by the global \bwater\b token - accepted, conservative.

label: Fresh Bean Sprouts
note: Requires the full 'bean sprout(s)' phrase, so Brussels sprouts (existing brussels-sprouts includes 'brussels? sprouts?' and cannot match 'bean sprouts') and broccoli sprouts are out by construction; brussels/alfalfa excluded belt-and-suspenders. 'la choy' blocks the canned brand whose title may omit the word canned; 'sprouted' blocks sprouted-grain bread.

label: Broccolini / Baby Broccoli
note: HIJACK FLAG: existing 'broccoli' includes unanchored 'broccoli', which substring-matches 'broccolini' and phrase-matches 'baby broccoli' - broccoli steals every broccolini product today; fix in collisions-b.md. This rule cannot steal back: plain broccoli crowns/bunches contain none of these tokens.

label: Fennel Bulb
note: Existing 'ground-fennel' (fennel seed/ground fennel) already excludes \bbulb\b and 'fresh fennel' - clean mutual boundary. Bare-title produce ('Fennel' / 'Fennel, each') caught by the start-anchored patterns without opening the door to 'fennel seed' spice jars; seed/ground/pollen/tea excluded anyway. Anise NOT used as a token (star anise is a spice).

label: Chayote Squash
note: 'chayote' is a unique produce word; no existing commodity references it and zucchini's 'yellow squash' include cannot match it. Minimal excludes suffice on top of the global prepared-food wall.

label: Yuca / Cassava Root
note: Both spellings covered ('yuca' and 'yucca root'); bare '\byucca\b' avoided (garden-plant listings). Cassava flour/starch/chips and tapioca 'pearls' excluded; frozen yuca and yuca fries excluded. No existing commodity carries any of these tokens.

label: Jicama
note: Whole root only: pre-cut sticks (usually chile-lime seasoned; 'seasoned' is also global-blocked), jicama chips, slaw, and jicama tortilla-wraps excluded. Unique word, no existing-commodity overlap.

label: Fresh Okra
note: Per lesson: does NOT require the word 'fresh' (stores title it plain 'Okra'). Frozen breaded/cut okra, pickled jars, canned okra & tomatoes, and gumbo blends excluded (frozen/canned/breaded are also global). No existing commodity matches 'okra'.

label: Artichokes (fresh, whole)
note: Candidate notes: hearts are NOT wanted here - existing 'artichoke-hearts' owns canned/jarred/marinated hearts and sits earlier in the file (first-match protects it), plus hearts/quarters/marinated/jarred excluded here explicitly. 'fresh' not required in include (stores title plain 'Artichoke'). artichoke-hearts already excludes \bfresh\b + \bfrozen\b so a title like 'Fresh Artichoke' can't be stolen; a bare 'Artichoke Hearts' title is include-blocked here both by order and exclude.

label: Fresh Rhubarb
note: Per lesson: 'fresh' not required in include. 'strawberry' excluded because virtually every processed rhubarb product is strawberry-rhubarb (pie/jam/yogurt); plain fresh stalks are titled 'Rhubarb'. Frozen rhubarb excluded (also global). No existing commodity overlap.

label: Pie Pumpkins
note: Adjacent phrases 'pie pumpkin'/'sugar pumpkin'/'baking pumpkin' only - 'pumpkin pie mix/filling' is reversed word order and cannot match, and existing canned-pumpkin (100%/pure/puree/solid-pack anchored, excludes \bpie\b) is disjoint in both directions. Carving/jack-o-lantern pumpkins and pumpkin-spice products excluded.

label: Fresh Parsley (bunch)
note: HIJACK FLAG: existing 'dried-parsley' includes bare 'parsley' and only excludes fresh/bunch/plant/living/curly-bunch - titles like 'Italian Parsley' or 'Flat Leaf Parsley' (no 'fresh', no 'bunch') are stolen by the spice item today; fix in collisions-b.md. This rule cannot steal dried products: spice jars are titled 'Parsley Flakes'/'Parsley' and match none of these phrases; dried/flakes excluded regardless. 'cilantro' guards combo two-bunch packs.

note: CRITICAL boundary: existing 'pickles' includes 'dill spears'/'pickle(s)' - my includes require fresh/bunch/clamshell/sprig context so no pickle jar can enter, and pickles?/pickled excluded anyway. Havarti (dill cheese) and dill dip/ranch guarded.

label: Fresh Rosemary
note: No dried-rosemary commodity exists, so there is no hijack partner - but a spice jar titled just 'Rosemary' must not enter here, hence includes are anchored on fresh/clamshell/bunch/sprig and dried/ground/seasoning excluded. RISK (accepted, conservative): a fresh pack titled bare 'Rosemary 0.75 oz' will be missed until real store titles are captured. Scented/candle/soap/oil block the toiletry aisle.

label: Fresh Thyme
note: HIJACK FLAG: existing 'dried-thyme' includes bare '\bthyme\b' (excludes only fresh/plant/living/seeds), so a produce clamshell titled 'Thyme 0.75 oz' or 'Organic Thyme' is stolen by the spice item today; fix in collisions-b.md. Includes anchored fresh/clamshell/bunch/sprig so this rule can never steal a spice jar; bare-'Thyme' titles remain ambiguous either way and stay with dried-thyme (accepted, conservative).
